answer.summary: Campbell said the mistake was blaming an employee for poor performance when leadership had not clearly defined what good performance looked like or kept talking with them about expectations and what they needed to succeed.

sections.heading: The management mistake
sections.content: When someone failed to ship at the expected pace, Campbell said leaders often treated it as an employee problem—甚至 questioning the hire—instead of recognizing it as an organizational problem. They had not set a clear expectation for what good tempo looked like or maintained conversations to check that the employee had what they needed. That ambiguity could create misalignment, friction, and resentment; he recommended agreeing on the expected output and asking why any gap remained so it could be addressed.
